en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The aim of the course is to introduce students to the principles of modern analytical methods and their instrumentation. Students will also be introduced to practical analytical applications.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Introduction to the instrumental methods (allowance 2/0)2.Atomic absorption spectrophotometry (allowance 2/0)3.Optical methods (allowance 2/0)4.Spectrophotometry (allowance 4/0) a.Spectrophotometry in the UV/VIS region.b.Spectrophotometry in the IR region.5.Nuclear magnetic resonance (allowance 2/0)6.Mass spectrometry (allowance 2/0)7.Ambient techniques (allowance 2/0)8.Electromigration methods (allowance 2/0)9.Electrophoresis (allowance 2/0)10.Separation methods (allowance 2/0)11.Liquid chromatography (allowance 2/0)12.Gas chromatography (allowance 2/0)13.Automation in instrumental analytical techniques (allowance 2/0)14.Practical laboratory exercises (allowance 28/0) a.Introduction to the exercises, good laboratory practice.b.Sample preparation, grinding, homogenisation, lyophilisation.c.Solid phase extraction, extraction of food colourings in beverages.d.Supercritical fluid extraction, extraction of essential oils in selected spices.e.Thin-layer chromatography of food colourings in beverages.f.Determination of polyphenols in selected tea species by liquid chromatography coupled to a detector diode array detector.g.Determination of resveratrol in wine by liquid chromatography coupled to a mass spectrometer.h.Gas chromatography, determination of lipoid acids in meat samples.
